chapter: Cross-references (Ch 3 §3.8, Ch 5 §5.8, Ch 7 §7.1 vs Preface convention)
evidence: Preface (p.19): "Do not repeat a chapter number after the chapter name — write Ch. 8 § 3 or § 8.3.3, not Ch. 8 § 8.3.3." Violations: p.79 "unless we explicitly use expert offload/swapping (Ch 3 §3.6, Ch 18)"; p.141 "less the ~64 GB runtime reserve that Ch 7 §7.3 subtracts" and "matching Ch 4 §4.6"; p.161 "and Ch 4 §4.7 tags the same quantity the same way".
issue: Four section cross-references use the exact form the book's own Preface convention prohibits (chapter number repeated after the chapter name: 'Ch N §N.M' instead of 'Ch N §M' or '§N.M'). The targets themselves exist and discuss the cited topics; only the reference form is malformed.
fix_instruction: Rewrite 'Ch 3 §3.6'→'§3.6', 'Ch 7 §7.3'→'Ch 7 §3' (or '§7.3'), 'Ch 4 §4.6'→'Ch 4 §6' (or '§4.6'), 'Ch 4 §4.7'→'Ch 4 §7' (or '§4.7'), per the Preface rule; sweep the rest of the book (incl. Ch 8–26 and Appendix A, not verifiable in this round) for the same 'Ch N §N.M' pattern.

chapter: Appendix A reference style (Ch 1 §1.1.2, Preface evidence-cutoff section, Ch 4 Table 4-2 box)
evidence: Preface (p.19): "Appendix A numbers its own sections with a letter suffix, so Appendix A § 9A means Appendix A, the section labelled 9A; the appendix's figures carry A.N." But: p.7 "...all accessed 2026-08-30, the book's evidence cutoff; Appendix A §10)"; p.21 "Appendix A, A.6 carries a boxed 2026-09-27 capability probe" and "a superseding re-verification of the DeepSeek model-service status (Appendix A, A.3)"; p.102 "Appendix A's §A.7 (Fig A.2, vendor-relative KV/compute ratios)".
issue: Internal inconsistency in Appendix A section-reference style: the stated convention is letter-suffixed section labels (§9A) with A.N reserved for figures, yet the book references appendix sections as '§10' (no letter suffix, p.7) and as 'A.6'/'A.3'/'§A.7' (figure-style labels used for sections, pp. 21, 102). A reader cannot tell whether 'A.6' denotes section 6, section 6A, or figure A.6 (which also exists per the List of Figures).
fix_instruction: Pick one appendix section-label scheme and enforce it: either relabel all section refs to the letter-suffixed form (§10A, §6A, §3A, §7A) or amend the Preface convention sentence to describe the actual mixed scheme, and rename figure refs to an unambiguous form (e.g., 'Fig A.2') wherever collision is possible. Verify against the appendix's own headings (pp. 482–514).

evidence: p.55: "(The symbol is Mweights, not W: throughout the book W is reserved for mean time in system in Little's law, L = λW, Ch 4.)" But L is also defined as sequence length: p.41 "the weight-matmul FLOPs, 2NL (where N = model parameters and L = tokens processed)"; p.128 "the attention term is 4·L·d_model·n_layers = 4 × 9,200 × 8,192 × 80"; p.149 "M_history(L) = L × 65,536 bytes". Little's-law use of bare L: p.107 "Little's Law, L = λW, relates the average number of requests in the defined system L"; p.110 "L (in-flight requests)".
issue: The book explicitly reserves W (and disambiguates Mweights) but double-books L: sequence length/tokens processed in the FLOP and history-state formulas (Ch 1 §1.1.4, Ch 2, Ch 6 §6.3.3, Ch 7 §7.3.2) vs in-flight request count in Little's law (Ch 4 §4.3 walk-through). The Ch 4 usage is mostly mitigated by the Lexec subscript, but the bare 'L = λW' statements collide with the FLOP-formula L across chapters.
fix_instruction: Reserve a distinct symbol for the Little's-law in-flight count (e.g., N_inflight or Q) or restrict bare-L Little's-law statements to 'Lexec = λ × Wexec'; add L to the reservation note on p.55 alongside W.

evidence: p.177: "The same caution applies to safetensors: storing tensors in a recognized container does not establish that a loader understands their quantized schema. [1P][DERIVED] (GGUF specification, pinned revision, retrieved 2026-10-28)." Book definition (p.16): "DERIVED — computed by arithmetic from stated inputs."
issue: Evidence-label mismatch: the tagged sentence is a reasoned caution about container/loader behavior, not a value computed by arithmetic from stated inputs, so [1P][DERIVED] does not match the book's own Axis-2 definition. The GGUF-spec facts earlier in the paragraph are [1P][FACT]-type content; the caution is the book's own inference.
fix_instruction: Retag: spec-content statements as [1P][FACT] (GGUF/safetensors specifications, pinned revisions), and the load-rejection caution as untagged reasoned guidance or [1P][HYPOTHESIS]; reserve [DERIVED] for arithmetic results.
